facts.text: History can be studied with the help of written sources, material sources, oral sources and sources in the audio-visual medium.
facts.quote: We can study history with the help of various sources like written sources, material sources, oral sources and sources in the audio-visual medium.

facts.text: In the modern period we have to take note of sources at the regional, state, national as well as international level.
facts.quote: In the modern period, we have to take note of various sources at the regional, state, national as well as international level.

facts.text: Written sources include newspapers, periodicals, diaries, reference books, correspondence, documents in the archives, government gazettes, postage stamps and encyclopedias.
facts.quote: Newspapers ... Periodicals ... Diaries ... Reference books ... Correspondence ... Documents in the Archives ... Government Gazettes ... Postage Stamps ... Encyclopedias

facts.text: The place where historical documents are preserved is called 'Archives'.
facts.quote: The place where historical documents are preserved is called 'Archives'.

facts.text: The main office of the National Archives of India is at New Delhi; it is the largest among the Archives in Asia.
facts.quote: The main office of the National Archives of India is at New Delhi. It is the largest among the Archives in Asia.

facts.text: Newspapers are considered the fourth pillar of democracy in the modern period.
facts.quote: Just as newspapers are considered the fourth pillar of democracy in the modern period, they are also a major medium of information.

facts.text: From 1961 to 2000, at first there was no alternative to print media; with liberalisation and widespread use of internet an alternative became available, yet print media still continue to be powerful.
facts.quote: If we consider the period from 1961 to 2000, we see that in the beginning, there was no alternative to the print media, especially newspapers. With liberalisation and widespread use of internet in India, an alternative for print media became available. Yet, the print media still continue to be powerful.

facts.text: Most national newspapers have started their regional editions and publish supplements on various topics.
facts.quote: Most national newspapers have started their regional editions. They publish supplements that give information about various topics.

facts.text: Some newspapers produce special supplements towards the end of the year that take an overview of the important events of the year.
facts.quote: Some newspapers produce special supplements towards the end of the year that take an overview of the important events of the year.

facts.text: After 1953, the Press Trust of India (PTI) has been an important source of primary details of all important events.
facts.quote: After 1953, the Press Trust of India has been an important source of primary details of all important events and of articles on important subjects.

facts.text: PTI has provided reports, photographs and articles on financial and scientific issues to newspapers, and has now started its online service.
facts.quote: Press Trust of India has provided reports, photographs and articles on financial and scientific issues to newspapers. PTI has now started its online service.

facts.text: During the 1990s, PTI started using 'satellite broadcast' technology instead of tele-printers to send news all over the country.
facts.quote: During the 1990s, PTI started using the 'satellite broadcast' technology instead of tele-printers to send news all over the country.

facts.text: Information in the annual issues of the Publications Division of the Government of India is authentic and trustworthy.
facts.quote: Among the print media, the information contained in the annual issues of the Publications Division of the Government of India is authentic and trustworthy.

facts.text: The Information and Broadcasting Department published INDIA 2000, an annual reference book created under the 'Research, Reference and Training Department'.
facts.quote: the Information and Broadcasting Department published INDIA 2000, an annual reference book. This reference book is created under 'Research, Reference and Training Department'.

facts.text: INDIA 2000 contains information about the land, its people, national emblems, political system, defence, education and much basic data on economics, agriculture, energy, transport and more.
facts.quote: It contains useful information about the land, its people, national emblems, political system, defence, education, ... along with basic data, related to economics, finance, planning, agriculture, ... energy, industries, trade and commerce, transport ...

facts.text: Postage stamps don't reveal anything on their own, yet a historian makes them speak; their sizes, subjects and colour schemes reveal changing times.
facts.quote: The postage stamps don't reveal anything on their own. Yet a historian makes them speak. ... Postage stamps reveal a lot to us about changing times due to the variety in the sizes of the stamps, the novelty in their subjects and colour schemes.

facts.text: The Postal Department issues stamps on themes like political leaders, flowers, animals, birds, events and silver, golden, diamond jubilees, centenary, bicentenary and tercentenary; it is a valuable repository of history.
facts.quote: The Postal Department issues postage stamps on a wide variety of themes like political leaders, flowers, animals, birds, an event, or the silver, golden, diamond jubilees or centenary, bicentenary, tercentenary of different events. It is therefore a valuable repository of history.

facts.text: The Indian government issued the 'Jal Cooper' stamp in 1977.
facts.quote: The Indian government issued the 'Jal Cooper' stamp in 1977.

facts.text: Jal Cooper was an internationally acclaimed philatelist (an expert on postage stamps), born in a Parsi household in Mumbai, who edited 'India's Stamp Journal'.
facts.quote: Jal Cooper was an internationally acclaimed philatelist, i.e. an expert on the subject of 'postage stamps'. Born in a Parsi household in Mumbai, Cooper edited 'India's Stamp Journal'.

facts.text: Jal Cooper founded the first Philatelic Bureau in India (an office that collected stamps) and the 'Empire of India Philatelic Society', and wrote many books on stamps.
facts.quote: He was the founder of the first Philatelic Bureau in India, an office that collected stamps. He founded the 'Empire of India Philatelic Society'. He went on to write many books on this subject.

facts.text: Material sources include coins, places of worship, things in daily use, royal seals, ornaments, museums, clothing and modern architecture.
facts.quote: Coins ... Places of worship ... Things in daily use ... Royal Seals ... Ornaments ... Museums ... Clothing ... Modern architecture

facts.text: The Reserve Bank of India prints the notes; it has its headquarters in Mumbai.
facts.quote: Reserve Bank of India prints the notes. It has its headquarters in Mumbai.

facts.text: The coins from 1950 to the present help us understand contemporary issues in India, e.g. coins conveying population control and the importance of agriculture and farmers.
facts.quote: The coins from 1950 to those used at present, the metals used for making them, their different shapes, the diversity of subjects on them together help us to understand the important contemporary issues in India eg., coins to convey the message of population control and coins communicating the importance of agriculture and of farmers.

facts.text: All States of India have museums; an example is the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Museum at Mumbai. Private collectors also set up museums on subjects like coins, notes, lamps, nutcrackers and cricket equipment.
facts.quote: All States of India have museums ... (eg., the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Museum at Mumbai. Apart from the Government Museums, some private collectors also set up their own museums. ... eg., coins, notes, lamps and nutcrackers in different shapes, cricket equipment, etc.

facts.text: Oral sources include folktales, folksongs, proverbs, ballads and owis (Marathi verses in the oral tradition).
facts.quote: Oral sources : These sources include folktales, folksongs, proverbs, ballads and owis (Marathi verses in the oral tradition).

facts.text: Activists were inspired by the powadas of Lokshahir Anna Bhau Sathe and Shahir Amar Sheikh during the Sanyukta Maharashtra Movement.
facts.quote: Activists were inspired by the powadas of Lokshahir Anna Bhau Sathe and Shahir Amar Sheikh during the Sanyukta Maharashtra Movement.

facts.text: The noted Marathi poet Kusumagraj wrote the poem 'Aavahan' on the backdrop of the Sino-Indian war.
facts.quote: study the poem 'Aavahan' written on the backdrop of the Sino-Indian war by the noted Marathi poet Kusumagraj.

facts.text: Television, films and internet are called 'Audio-visual media'; channels like History channel and Discovery channel also come under this head.
facts.quote: Television, films, internet are called 'Audio-visual media'. Many domestic and foreign television channels also come under this head, eg., History channel, Discovery channel, etc.

facts.text: The Government of India started the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII) at Pune in 1960 with the purpose of providing public education.
facts.quote: The Government of India started the Film and Television Institute of India at Pune in 1960 with the purpose of providing public education.

facts.text: An institute called Indian News Review produced newsreels on important events in politics, social issues, art, sports and culture; documentaries were also made on social leaders and important locations.
facts.quote: An institute called Indian News Review has produced various newsreels on important events in politics, social issues, art, sports and culture. This Department has also produced various documentaries on prominent social leaders, on people who have made major contributions for the country and about important locations in India.

facts.text: During the change from land line telephones to cellphones, a gadget called 'pager' came up for contacting people but died out as quickly as it had come up.
facts.quote: during the transformation from land line telephone to cellphones, a gadget called 'pager' came up for contacting people. But it died out as quickly as it had come up.

facts.text: The huge amount of information on the Internet is used for studying history, but its truth and authenticity need to be verified.
facts.quote: The huge amount of information available on the Internet is used for studying history, but the truth and authenticity of this information needs to be verified.

facts.text: Modern sources are from the contemporary period, so they are easily available; efforts to preserve them are made at all levels.
facts.quote: As these sources are from the contemporary period, they are easily available. Since a subject like history touches all the aspects of our lives, efforts for preservation of such sources are made at all levels.
